cohort: Seventy-one pregnant women (38 with GDM, 33 non-GDM) and their newborns were enrolled; the GDM group was further stratified into those requiring insulin therapy (n=8) and those managed by diet alone (n=30).
finding: Pretreatment, pregnant women who later required insulin for GDM showed higher proportions of Clostridiales, Lactobacillus, and Bacteroidetes in their gut microbiota; post-treatment, insulin therapy changed maternal gut microbiota composition, and these changes could be transferred to their newborns.
followup_time: Mothers were followed from GDM diagnosis (24-28 weeks gestation) until before delivery (>=37 weeks gestation); newborn samples were collected immediately after birth.
gest_age: Maternal samples were collected at GDM diagnosis (24-28 weeks gestation) and before delivery (>=37 weeks gestation), implying newborns were term.
